To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
late pregnancy supplementation of hair sheep with a high-energy-protein diet improved both cotyledon development (NC and DC) and litter weight at lambing, even under a severe heat stress condition.

the nutritional supplementation of hair ewes, besides to an increase in energy body reserves (weight and body condition) also improved both number and size of placental cotylodes, and generated an increased litter birth weight.

the divergent nutrition level during late pregnancy, along with severe heat stress conditions, affected the physiological variables and the placental cotyledon development in hair ewes, while the litter weight at birth increased.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of late pregnancy nutrition level upon some physiological variables, placental development, and litter weight at lambing in hair sheep under heat stress conditions.

a better understanding of the physiological mechanisms that occur in the hair sheep during the last weeks of pregnancy and how they are influenced by the nutritional plane, which may have important implications for the future of hair sheep production systems.
the effects of heat stress and nutritional restriction upon the placental development and litter size at birth in hair sheep.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the observed heat stress conditions in this study did not affect negatively to the placental development and litter weight, but rather the increased energy-protein diet in the NNR treatment improved the number and size (DC) of the cotyledons along the gestation, which was reflected on an increased litter weight.
the observed NNR effects were exerted as a result of the increased energy-protein intake and not as a direct consequence of a lower heat stress level.
a nutritional supplementation of ewes during the last third of the gestation period is beneficial to the development of the placenta, and therefore, to the newborns.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a nutritionally supplemented diet in heat-stressed ewes during late pregnancy could help to improve the litter size and weight at birth.

the nutritional supplementation in late pregnancy of hair ewes facing severe heat stress, not only increased the energy body reserves but also improved the placental cotyledon development along with litter weight.

nutritional supplementation in late pregnancy in hair ewes, even when they face severe heat stress conditions, improves both the placental development and litter weight, which are two key factors for the lambing performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
nutritional supplementation in heat-stressed hair sheep is a key factor to improve both litter weight at birth and the number and size placental cotyledon.
hair sheep ewes under severe heat stress conditions and late pregnancy, can benefit from a nutritional supplementation to improve the litter size and weight at birth.

the nutritional supplementation during late pregnancy in hair ewes, besides to an increase of energy reserves in the body, also improved the number and size (area) of the cotyledons and the litter weight at birth, which could be of great importance for hair ewes breeders.
